nodes.label: DHT22 / AM2302 Temperature and Humidity Sensor Module
nodes.description: Close-up photograph of a red breakout PCB silkscreened 'AM2302 DHT22 Sensor' carrying a white slotted plastic sensor housing marked 'AOSONG AM2302 SN17023IEEC'. A right-angle 3-pin male header exits the right edge, with the pads labelled DAT, VCC and GND on the silkscreen; two mounting holes and a pull-up resistor pad are visible. This is the actual hardware component used in the build, photographed as equipment documentation.
nodes.rationale: The 3-pin DAT/VCC/GND breakout is preferred over the bare 4-pin sensor because the pull-up resistor is already populated on the board, so it wires straight to a single-board-computer GPIO header with three jumper wires and no extra components.

nodes.label: Single-Wire DAT/VCC/GND Digital Interface
nodes.description: The module's electrical contract: power, ground and a single bidirectional data line carrying a digital temperature and relative-humidity reading.
nodes.rationale: A digital single-wire protocol removes the need for analogue-to-digital conversion, which matters because the Raspberry Pi has no on-board ADC.

nodes.label: Ambient Temperature and Humidity Monitoring
nodes.description: Continuous measurement of poultry-house air temperature and relative humidity as the environmental context signal for welfare assessment.
nodes.rationale: Humidity is measured alongside temperature because evaporative cooling by panting fails at high relative humidity, so temperature alone under-states the true thermal load on the birds.
